chunks: Al-Shaykh, may Allah the Exalted support him, informed me from Abū al-Ḥasan Muḥammad ibn Aḥmad ibn Dāwūd, from his father, from Abū al-Ḥasan ʿAlī ibn al-Ḥusayn, from Muḥammad ibn Yaḥyā, from Muḥammad ibn Aḥmad ibn Yaḥyā, from Abū ʿAbdillāh al-Rāzī, from Aḥmad ibn Muḥammad ibn Abī Naṣr, from Ismāʿīl, who said: Abū al-Ḥasan al-Dallāl narrated to me from Yaḥyā ibn ʿAbdillāh, who said: I heard Abā ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام say:

‘What prevents the family of your deceased from warding off from their dead one the encounter with Munkar and Nakīr?’ He said: I said, ‘How should we do that?’ He said: ‘When the deceased has been left alone, let the person closest to him remain by him, place his mouth near his head, then call out in the loudest voice: O so-and-so son of so-and-so, or O so-and-so daughter of so-and-so, are you upon the covenant upon which you parted from us: the testimony that there is no god but Allah alone, without partner, and that Muḥammad is His servant and His Messenger, the master of the Prophets, and that ʿAlī is Amīr al-Muʾminīn and the master of the legatees, and that what Muḥammad brought is true, and that death is true, and resurrection is true, and that Allah, Exalted is He,
‘will raise those who are in the graves.’
He said: ‘Then Munkar will say to Nakīr: Let us turn away from this one, for he has been instructed in his proof.’

And al-Shaykh informed us of this hadith from Abū al-Qāsim Jaʿfar ibn Muḥammad, from Muḥammad ibn Yaʿqūb, from Muḥammad ibn Yaḥyā, from some of our companions, from Aḥmad ibn Muḥammad ibn Abī Naṣr, from Ismāʿīl, who said: Abū al-Ḥasan al-Dallāl narrated to me from Yaḥyā ibn ʿAbdillāh, who said: I heard Abā ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام say: the like of that.

Al-Shaykh, may Allah the Exalted support him, said: It is disliked that water be heated by fire for the ghusl of the deceased; but if it is winter and the cold is severe, then let a little be warmed for him so that the one washing him may be able to wash him.

key_terms.أَمِيرُ اَلْمُؤْمِنِينَ: title of ʿAlī عليه السلام in the formula of talqin
key_terms.حُجَّتَهُ: his proof or answer with which he responds
key_terms.شَهَادَةِ: the testimony of faith affirmed for the deceased
key_terms.غُسْلِ اَلْمَيِّتِ: the ritual washing of the deceased
key_terms.مُنْكَرٍ وَنَكِيرٍ: the two angels associated with questioning in the grave

ai.seo_question: How should the deceased be given talqin in Shia hadith, and what does it mean for Munkar and Nakīr?
ai.summary: This hadith teaches the talqin of the deceased after burial, reminding the dead of the testimony of tawhid, the رسالَة of Muḥammad صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم, the wilayah of ʿAlī عليه السلام, and the realities of death and resurrection. It also states that such prompting serves as the deceased’s proof before Munkar and Nakīr, and it includes a related legal note that heating water for the ghusl of the deceased is disliked unless severe cold requires it.
